name: Baseline (constant rates)
description: The smooth path used by the main model: constant growth every year. Real economies never behave this way — included only as a comparison.
home_price_pattern: Property A +4%/yr and Property B +3%/yr every year (assumption)

name: Historical replay 1976-2025 -> 2026-2075
description: The 50 actual annual CPI inflation rates of 1976-2025 (BLS) are re-run year by year over 2026-2075. Home-price real growth follows the actual era pattern (booms recessions and one -35% crash); portfolio returns carry crash and rebound years.
cpi_pattern: Actual BLS CPI-U annual averages 1976-2025 applied 2026-2075 (verified series)
portfolio_pattern: 4.5% + 0.5x(CPI-2.5%) nominal per year with -37% (2008-pattern year) and +26% rebounds in the crash window (assumption)

name: Stagflation replay (1974-1983 pattern)
description: A decade where inflation runs 4-13% per year mortgage rates spike and home prices only keep up with inflation in nominal terms (deep real losses). Taxes and insurance inflate fast.
home_price_pattern: +2%/yr nominal during the shock window (1970s pattern: nominal gains real losses) then A +4% B +3% (assumption)
portfolio_pattern: +5%/yr nominal during the shock (1970s stocks flat in real terms) then 7% (assumption)

name: Great Financial Crisis replay (2007-2012 pattern)
description: A repeat of the Bay Area crash: home values fall about 35% peak-to-trough over five years a two-year stock crash and brief deflation — landing exactly around the inheritance window.
home_price_pattern: -8.2%/yr for 5 years (compounds to about -35% the SF all-transactions peak-to-trough) then +8%/yr recovery for 5 years (derived from FHFA HPI episode H6)

name: Japan-style deflation (tail)
description: Fifteen years of falling or flat home values with near-zero inflation and stagnant equities. Extreme tail case: Japanese major-city land fell for more than a decade after 1991 (historical episode; magnitude here is a moderate -2%/yr assumption not a forecast).

name: COVID-shock pattern (2020-2023)
description: A four-year whiplash: a demand boom (+18% home values) an 8% inflation year a rate shock that cools prices and a stock crash and rebound — the exact 2020-2023 sequence.
cpi_pattern: 2.5% until 2035; 2036-2039 = actual 2020-2023 CPI (1.2 4.7 8.0 4.1); 2.8% after (verified CPI segment)
